subject: GK
text: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India?
explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru served as the first Prime Minister of India from its independence in 1947 until his death in 1964.

subject: GK
text: Which animal is designated as the National Animal of India?
explanation: The Royal Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris) was declared the national animal of India in April 1972, replacing the lion, to promote tiger conservation.

subject: GK
text: Which is the highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world?
explanation: Angel Falls, located in Venezuela, is the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, with a height of 979 meters (3,212 feet).

subject: GK
text: What is the capital city of France?
explanation: Paris is the capital and most populous city of France, situated on the Seine River in the north-central part of the country.

subject: GK
text: Which gas is the most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere by volume?
explanation: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in the atmosphere, making up approximately 78% of the air we breathe, followed by oxygen at 21%.

subject: GK
text: Who is credited with inventing the telephone in 1876?
explanation: Alexander Graham Bell was awarded the first US patent for the telephone in 1876, establishing the Bell Telephone Company.

subject: GK
text: In which year was the 'Quit India Movement' launched by Mahatma Gandhi, demanding an end to British rule?
explanation: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement (August Kranti Movement) at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee on 8 August 1942.

subject: GK
text: Which organ in the human body is primarily responsible for filtering waste from the blood and producing urine?
explanation: The kidneys filter blood to remove metabolic wastes, excess salts, and water, excreting them in the form of urine.

subject: GK
text: Which is the largest state in India by geographic land area?
explanation: Rajasthan is the largest state in India by area, covering 342,239 square kilometers, which is about 10.4% of the country's total land area.

subject: GK
text: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in which year?
explanation: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948 in Paris, establishing fundamental human rights to be universally protected.

subject: GK
text: Which country is globally referred to as the 'Sugar Bowl of the World' due to its massive sugar production?
explanation: Cuba was historically nicknamed the Sugar Bowl of the World as it was the largest exporter of sugar, though Brazil and India have now surpassed it in production.

subject: GK
text: What does the standard economic indicator abbreviation 'GDP' stand for?
explanation: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, which represents the total monetary or market value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.

subject: GK
text: Who founded the reformist social movement 'Brahmo Samaj' in Calcutta in 1828?
explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 to fight social evils like Sati, child marriage, and caste discrimination, promoting monotheism and rationalism.

subject: GK
text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution grants the Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and its procedures?
explanation: Article 368 of Part XX of the Indian Constitution details the power of Parliament to amend the constitution by way of addition, variation, or repeal.

subject: GK
text: Which is the longest river in the world, flowing northwards through northeastern Africa?
explanation: The Nile River is traditionally considered the longest river in the world, stretching about 6,650 kilometers (4,132 miles) and flowing into the Mediterranean Sea.

subject: GK
text: Who was the first Indian (and Asian) to receive a Nobel Prize, winning it in the Literature category in 1913?
explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his collection of poems 'Gitanjali', becoming the first non-European to win the award.

subject: GK
text: Which city is the federal capital of Australia?
explanation: Canberra was selected as the capital city of Australia in 1908 as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

subject: GK
text: Which national football team won the FIFA Men's World Cup in 2022?
explanation: Argentina won the 2022 FIFA World Cup hosted in Qatar, defeating France in a dramatic penalty shootout in the final.

subject: GK
text: Under whose viceroyalty was the highly controversial 'Vernacular Press Act' of 1878 enacted to muzzle regional newspapers?
explanation: Lord Lytton passed the Vernacular Press Act of 1878 to suppress local-language newspapers that criticized British policies. It was later repealed by Lord Ripon in 1882.

subject: GK
text: Who was appointed as the first Chief Election Commissioner of independent India, overseeing the first two general elections?
explanation: Sukumar Sen, an Indian civil servant, served as the first Chief Election Commissioner of India from 1950 to 1958, managing the massive 1951-52 and 1957 elections.

subject: GK
text: Which narrow sea strait separates the main continent of Australia from the island state of Tasmania?
explanation: The Bass Strait is a body of water that separates Tasmania from the Australian mainland (the state of Victoria) and connects the Tasman Sea to the Indian Ocean.

subject: GK
text: Which economic indicator calculates the total value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents and businesses, regardless of the production location?
explanation: Gross National Product (GNP) measures the total value of goods and services produced by a nation's citizens, including those residing abroad, but excluding foreign residents living within the nation.

subject: GK
text: The 'Dampa Tiger Reserve', which is a rich biosphere reserve hosting cloud leopards and rare bird species, is located in which Indian state?
explanation: Dampa Tiger Reserve is located in the Mamit district of Mizoram along the border with Bangladesh, covering an area of 500 square kilometers.

subject: GK
text: Which Russian chemist is credited with formulating the Periodic Law and creating the first version of the Periodic Table of Elements in 1869?
explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the chemical elements by atomic weight, predicting the properties of elements that were yet to be discovered, which revolutionized chemical science.

subject: GK
text: The 'Simla Accord' of 1972 was signed between India and Pakistan to define the Line of Control. Who signed this historic agreement on behalf of Pakistan?
explanation: The Simla Accord was signed on 2 July 1972 in Shimla by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi of India and President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto of Pakistan.
